## Root cause (investigated — the fix needs an operator decision)

`8f7417079ad` ("Restore Bedrock spend cap Terraform") restored the subsystem by path-checkout from
an unmerged branch and deliberately scrubbed the values out of the public tree. In doing so it
converted what the README still describes as **locals** into **required variables with no default**
and no value source. `infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/README.md:51` still refers to
`local.bedrock_cap_seed_rates`, which is the fingerprint of that conversion.

The root module has 16 variables. Exactly 4 lack a `default`, and they are exactly the 4 the plan
errors on:

- `bedrock_daily_cap_usd`, `bedrock_warn_threshold_usd`, `bedrock_cap_seed_rates`,
  `bedrock_cap_unknown_rate_per_1k` — all in `infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:31-66`.

The drift workflow supplies nothing to fill them: there is no `TF_VAR_`, no `-var-file`, and no
`tfvars` anywhere under `.github/` or `infra/terraform/`, and no `*.auto.tfvars` is tracked.
So `terraform plan` cannot be evaluated at all — the workflow's own summary text is correct that
this is "NOT drift", it is an unevaluable configuration.

### Why a guessed default is actively dangerous here

`infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf:215` builds the budget's **name** from the value:
`name = format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd)`. The live budget in
896586841071 is `bedrock-daily-500`. A default that does not match live would not merely be
cosmetically wrong — it would plan a destroy/recreate of the production spend cap, and applying it
would change the cap that is protecting the account. So "just add defaults" is not a safe
mechanical fix.

### No value store exists yet

Checked directly:

- SSM holds only `/bedrock-spend-cap/state` (the Lambda's runtime state), not these config values.
- GitHub Actions secrets are `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `GERRIT_SSH_PRIVKEY`, `JIRA_API_TOKEN`,
  `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY` — none carries the cap configuration.

The true values are recoverable from the live account (the `bedrock-spend-cap` Lambda's
environment carries `THRESHOLD_USD`, `WARN_THRESHOLD_USD`, `SEED_RATES`, `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`),
so any chosen option can be populated exactly, with zero planned change to live infrastructure.

### Why this needs a decision rather than a patch

This repository is **public**. Restoring the values to the tree reverses a deliberate scrubbing
decision. Every remaining option requires creating a value store that does not exist yet, and that
is an operator's call on a production spend control — so I am not choosing it unilaterally, and I
will not use a force override to move past it.

Options, all populated from the live values so the plan converges with no infrastructure change:

1. Publish the values as `default`s in `bedrock_spend_cap.tf`. Simplest and portable; reverses the
   scrubbing decision on a public repo.
2. Add `TF_VAR_*` to the drift workflow from new GitHub Actions secrets. Keeps the tree clean;
   ties the capability to GitHub Actions, which sits poorly with `project.portability`.
3. Publish the values into SSM and read them with `data "aws_ssm_parameter"` in the module. Keeps
   the tree clean, works for local applies and any CI with AWS credentials; changes the module's
   apply-time contract.

Blocked on that choice. Escalating rather than guessing.
